query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing the particle velocity by optimizing the HVAF-i7 torch’s nozzle configuration—specifically by selecting a spray distance in the 300–350 mm range—will overcome the thickness limitation for FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy bond coats.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powders with feedstock sizes of 15–45 μm, as used with the HVAF-i7 system yielding acceptable coating quality but insufficient thickness.
generation.intervention: Adjust the HVAF-i7 process parameters to operate at a higher in‐flight particle velocity by tuning the nozzle and setting the spray distance to approximately 300–350 mm.
generation.conditions: Deposition using the HVAF-i7 torch on substrates—including internal diameters as small as 120 mm—under elevated-temperature service conditions, similar to those in prior studies on conventional MCrAlY bond coats.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced in‐flight kinetic energy of powder particles leading to improved impact, deformation, and substrate splat formation.
generation.mechanism: Increasing the particle velocity increases kinetic energy which enhances particle flattening and bonding upon impact, promoting a denser, thicker coating buildup while retaining coating adherence and minimizing oxidation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Coatings deposited with the higher particle velocity are expected to achieve greater thickness relative to the baseline 15–45 μm-feedstock HVAF-i7 deposit, while maintaining acceptable levels of oxidation and adhesion.
generation.baseline: Coatings produced using 15–45 μm feedstock with the standard HVAF-i7 setting, which yield acceptable quality but insufficient coating thickness.
generation.boundary: This improvement is anticipated to hold within the operational limits of the HVAF-i7 system and for bond coat applications in restricted geometries (down to 120 mm OD) and high-temperature service; extreme parameter deviations or alterations in feedstock size may alter the outcome.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of the thickness increase and its potential interactions with coating oxidation and microstructure integrity are not fully defined and require empirical confirmation.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a controlled experiment comparing two HVAF-i7 depositions using the same FeCoNiCrAl feedstock (15–45 μm): one set with the standard spray parameters and one with the nozzle adjusted to achieve a spray distance of 300–350 mm (enhanced particle velocity). Ensure all other variables are held constant. Evaluate the thickness, adhesion, microstructure, and as-sprayed oxidation of the coatings.
measurements: Oxidation levels (using XPS or EDS analysis)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the adjusted HVAF-i7 settings fail to achieve a statistically significant increase in coating thickness without compromising adhesion or oxidation resistance compared with the standard process, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
## Abstract
Despite intense research on high entropy films, the mechanism of film growth and the influence of key factors remain incompletely understood. In this study, high entropy films consisting of five elements (FeCoNiCrAl) with columnar and nanometer-scale grains were prepared by magnetron sputtering. The high entropy film growth mechanism, including the formation of the amorphous domain, equiaxial nanocrystalline structure and columnar crystal was clarified by analyzing the microstructure in detail. Besides, the impacts of the important deposition parameters including the substrate temperature, the powder loaded in the target, and the crystal orientation of the substrate on the grain size and morphology, phase structure, crystallinity and elemental uniformity were revealed. The mechanical properties of high entropy films with various microstructure features were investigated by nanoindentation. With the optimized grain size and microstructure, the film deposited at 350 °C using a power of 100 W exhibits the highest hardness of 11.09 GPa. Our findings not only help understanding the mechanisms during the high entropy film deposition, but also provide guidance in manufacturing
